learning_outcomes.text: Acquire the fundamentals of the experimental method—common to all scientific disciplines—and the fundamental laws of classical mechanics and thermodynamics.
Acquire the necessary tools for a scientific approach to analyzing engineering problems.
Understand, analyze, and model engineering problems using acquired physics knowledge and methods.
Break down typically complex phenomena into their essential elements and apply the laws of classical physics to describe how they work.
Improve overall ability to exercise independent judgment.
Improve capacity to learn and draw conclusions.

syllabus_topics: Experimental method, physical quantities and measurements.
assessment_rules: The overall mark will be positive if at least 18 points are awarded in both the written test and the possible oral test. The final mark is obtained by mathematically averaging the mark in the written test and the mark in the oral test. Scores are in 30/30 scale, possibly with honors. For students with a disability/invalidity or specific learning disorder (DSA), the exam arrangements will be adapted in the light of the University guidelines.
